holidays.name: National TV Dinner Day
holidays.description: Peel back the foil and celebrate the frozen meal in a tray. It's the original heat-and-eat dinner, with a little compartment for every food and a dessert that sometimes ends up tasting like the main course.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance honoring the frozen TV dinner, which became a hit in the 1950s as television took over American living rooms. Swanson's 1953 turkey dinner is the best-known early version.
holidays.funFact: Swanson is said to have overestimated its Thanksgiving turkey supply in 1953 and ended up with roughly 260 tons of leftover birds. The frozen dinner was a clever way to use them up.

holidays.name: National Ants on a Log Day
holidays.description: Today is a salute to the classic snack of celery sticks filled with peanut butter and topped with a row of raisins. It's crunchy, creamy, sweet and a little bit silly. It's also a good way to get kids to eat their veggies.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. The snack itself is a longtime American lunchbox and after-school favorite. Its exact origins are unclear, but it has been a staple for decades.
holidays.funFact: Swap the raisins for chocolate chips and you get "ants on a log in the mud." Swap them for cranberries and you get "ladybugs on a log."

holidays.name: Blame It on the Large Hadron Collider Day
holidays.description: Today you get an official excuse for the day's misfortunes. Lost your keys, burned the toast, or got hit by a weird glitch? Blame it on the world's largest particle accelerator.
holidays.origin: This is a tongue-in-cheek observance tied to September 10, 2008. On that day, CERN's Large Hadron Collider near Geneva first circulated particle beams. Some people at the time worried it might cause catastrophe, which gave the day its joking spirit.
holidays.funFact: The Large Hadron Collider's main ring is about 27 kilometers (17 miles) around and sits roughly 100 meters (330 feet) underground. It's one of the largest machines ever built.
